rv.q: This magnificent revival of Arthur Miller’s study of real and allegorical witch hunts has grown in stature since it opened at the National Theatre nine months ago.
The entire production has an eerie, engulfing quality thanks to Es Devlin’s picture-perfect diorama of a set.
A magnificent revival, with a strong ensemble.
Transferring from the National Theatre, Lyndsey Turner's absorbing production succeeds triumphantly.
This production of The Crucible is well worth seeing, even if it’s a play you know as well as John Proctor knows his own name.
It's a watchable production of a great play, but it could have been so much more.
The play demands a powerful chemistry between them, but this is sadly lacking in their performance.
I have reached my verdict and my judgement is that this show really is devilishly good.
While certain aspects of this show ring true, it’s a shame that the production as a whole lacks enough emphasis on these to create a whole show worth revisiting.
Shining in some areas and dim in others, The Crucible is a show I’d recommend to lovers of classics.

cn.t: Turner's revival of Miller's classic earns praise for its staging and performances, though critics split on its overall impact. Devlin's water-drenched design impresses some as atmospheric, while others find it gimmicky in this uneven production.
